terms.definition: A three-dimensional composite block of tissue (skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, muscle, and bone) supplied anatomically by a single named source artery and drained by its accompanying veins (Taylor & Palmer, 1987).
terms.clinicalExample: Adjacent angiosomes are linked by choke vessels or true anastomoses; raising a flap across more than one choke-vessel boundary increases distal necrosis risk.

terms.definition: The unique vascular territory supplied by a single cutaneous perforator, connected to adjacent perforasomes via direct and indirect linking vessels (Saint-Cyr et al., 2009).
terms.clinicalExample: Flow within a perforasome preferentially follows the axiality of the limb or perpendicular to the midline on the trunk.

terms.definition: Reduced-caliber anastomotic arterioles connecting adjacent angiosomes or perforasomes that regulate flow across vascular territories and dilate permanently during the surgical delay phenomenon.
terms.clinicalExample: In a pedicled TRAM flap, superior epigastric inflow traverses choke vessels to perfuse the DIEA angiosome.

terms.definition: Subdermal and suprafascial vascular connections between adjacent perforasomes (Saint-Cyr). Direct linking vessels connect perforator-to-perforator directly; indirect linking vessels communicate via the subdermal plexus.
terms.clinicalExample: Oriented longitudinally in the extremities, allowing long elliptical skin paddles along the limb axis in ALT and fibula flaps.

terms.definition: Per the 2002 Gent Consensus, a vessel that pierces the deep fascia to supply the overlying subcutaneous tissue and skin. Subclassified as muscle perforators (musculocutaneous) or septal perforators (septocutaneous).
terms.clinicalExample: A DIEP flap is named after its source vessel (Deep Inferior Epigastric) rather than the traversed muscle (rectus abdominis).

terms.definition: The artery and accompanying vein(s) (venae comitantes or superficial vein) that supply and drain a flap.
terms.clinicalExample: The dominant pedicle of the ALT flap is the descending branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery with paired venae comitantes.

terms.definition: Paired deep veins running intimately alongside a deep source artery and communicating via cross-bridges, providing deep venous drainage for most extremity and perforator flaps.
terms.clinicalExample: In RFFF harvest, venous outflow can be via the deep venae comitantes, the superficial cephalic vein, or both.

terms.definition: The geometric sweep over which a pedicled flap can be transposed around its vascular pivot point without tension, kinking, or pedicle avulsion.
terms.clinicalExample: The medial gastrocnemius pivots on the medial sural pedicle to reach the anterior knee and proximal third of the tibia.

terms.definition: The fixed anatomical origin of the flap's vascular pedicle or skin base around which rotation or transposition occurs; effective reach decreases as the angle of rotation increases due to dog-ear tethering.
terms.clinicalExample: Dividing the humeral insertion of latissimus dorsi shifts the functional pivot point closer to the thoracodorsal hilum, extending anterior chest reach.

terms.definition: A composite flap consisting of multiple independent tissue components (e.g., skin paddle, muscle segment, bone) each supplied by separate branches arising from a single common source pedicle (Hallock).
terms.clinicalExample: Subscapular system chimeric flap combining latissimus dorsi muscle, serratus anterior, and parascapular skin on the subscapular artery.

terms.definition: An island flap based on a skeletonized eccentric perforator that rotates up to 180° like a propeller blade, placing the larger blade into the defect and the smaller blade toward the donor site (Tokyo Consensus, 2011).
terms.clinicalExample: Peroneal or posterior tibial artery perforator propeller flap for small-to-moderate distal leg defects.

terms.definition: A flap designed around any audible Doppler-mapped cutaneous perforator without pre-specifying the deep source vessel, traced retrograde until adequate pedicle length and caliber are achieved (Wei & Mardini).
terms.clinicalExample: Local V–Y or propeller resurfacing on the trunk or thigh using an adjacent high-signal Doppler perforator.

terms.definition: Axial flaps incorporate a named longitudinal arteriovenous system along their axis, enabling long length-to-width ratios; random flaps rely solely on the dermal–subdermal plexus and are constrained by base-to-length ratios.
terms.clinicalExample: Paramedian forehead (axial on supratrochlear artery) vs. cheek rhomboid transposition (random subdermal plexus).

terms.definition: A vascularized composite flap incorporating cortical/cancellous bone together with a skin paddle fed by periosteal or septocutaneous vessels from the same source artery.
terms.clinicalExample: Free fibula osteocutaneous flap for segmental mandibular or long-bone reconstruction.

terms.definition: A trapezoidal curvilinear fasciocutaneous island flap designed adjacent to an elliptical defect (1:1 width ratio, 90° lateral limbs) relying on random underlying musculocutaneous/fasciocutaneous perforators (Behan Types I–IV).
terms.clinicalExample: Type IIA (deep fascial division along the convex outer margin) closes moderate trunk or extremity oncologic wounds without microsurgery.

terms.definition: Prefabrication implants a new vascular pedicle beneath a desired donor tissue to neovascularize it before transfer. Prelamination grafts additional tissue layers (e.g., cartilage, mucosa) onto an existing axial flap before transfer.
terms.clinicalExample: Prelaminating a radial forearm flap with auricular cartilage and skin graft for subtotal nasal or tracheal reconstruction.

terms.definition: Staged partial devascularization (typically 10–14 days prior to transfer) that induces sympathectomy, permanent dilation of choke vessels, and longitudinal reorientation of microcirculation, increasing survivable flap length.
terms.clinicalExample: Ligation of the deep inferior epigastric vessels 2 weeks before a pedicled TRAM flap in high-risk patients.

terms.definition: Classification of lower abdominal skin perfusion across the midline in TRAM/DIEP flaps. Holm updated Hartrampf's scheme showing ipsilateral lateral tissue (Holm Zone II) often perfuses better than contralateral medial tissue (Holm Zone III).
terms.clinicalExample: Discarding Zone IV (contralateral lateral tip) prevents fat necrosis and distal skin loss in unilateral DIEP breast reconstruction.

terms.definition: The traditional ladder progresses from secondary intention → primary closure → skin graft → local flap → regional flap → free flap. The modern reconstructive elevator (Gottlieb & Krieger) selects the optimal rung directly based on form, function, and wound bed.
terms.clinicalExample: Moving directly to a free fibula osteocutaneous flap for an anterior segmental mandibular defect.

terms.definition: Relaxed Skin Tension Lines (RSTL) follow natural facial/body creases along minimal closing tension. The Line of Maximal Extensibility (LME) runs perpendicular to RSTL and represents the direction of greatest skin stretch.
terms.clinicalExample: Placing the short diagonal of a Limberg rhomboid flap parallel to the LME aligns the donor scar with RSTL.

terms.definition: Redundant triangular skin fold created at the pivot base of a rotation or transposition flap, excised as a Burow's triangle away from the vascular pedicle to allow flat contour inset.
terms.clinicalExample: Excising a small standing cone along the nasofacial sulcus during a Zitelli 90° bilobed nasal flap.

terms.definition: Bedside maneuver compressing both radial and ulnar arteries, exsanguinating the hand, and releasing the ulnar artery to verify intact palmar arch perfusion prior to radial artery harvest.
terms.clinicalExample: Capillary refill >6–10 seconds or abnormal Doppler signal suggests ulnar insufficiency and contraindicates RFFF harvest.

terms.definition: Congenital lower-extremity vascular anomaly in which a dominant peroneal artery supplies the foot while anterior and posterior tibial arteries are hypoplastic or absent (~0.2–5% incidence).
terms.clinicalExample: Absolute contraindication to free fibula harvest; ruled out via preoperative CTA or MRA runoff.

terms.definition: Supercharging augments a flap by anastomosing a distant source pedicle (e.g., SIEV to cephalic vein) to recipient vessels. Turbocharging anastomoses an additional pedicle within the flap to a branch of the primary pedicle.
terms.clinicalExample: Venous supercharging of a congested DIEP flap via the superficial inferior epigastric vein (SIEV).

terms.definition: A free or pedicled flap whose sensory nerve (for protective sensation) or motor nerve (for functional muscle transfer) is coapted to a recipient nerve.
terms.clinicalExample: Functional free gracilis muscle transfer coapted to the masseteric or cross-facial nerve for facial reanimation.

terms.definition: Ring-pin anastomotic device that everts venous intima-to-intima rapidly without intraluminal suture material, reducing ischemia time and thrombosis risk in venous anastomoses.
terms.clinicalExample: 2.5–3.0 mm venous coupler used for internal mammary or facial vein anastomosis in DIEP/ALT transfer.

terms.definition: Postoperative surveillance strategies for flaps without an external skin paddle (e.g., buried bone or hypopharyngeal flaps), including an externalized monitoring skin island, implantable Cook-Swartz Doppler, or near-infrared spectroscopy.
terms.clinicalExample: Placing an implantable 20-MHz Doppler probe on the venous pedicle of a buried free fibula.

terms.definition: The perimeter of perivascular inflammation, friable intima, and fibrosis extending beyond visible open fracture or radiation margins; microvascular anastomoses performed inside this zone carry elevated thrombosis risk.
terms.clinicalExample: Performing end-to-side anastomosis proximal to a Gustilo IIIB tibial fracture or utilizing arteriovenous loops / vein grafts.

mathes_nahai.examples: Gastrocnemius, Tensor fascia lata (TFL), Rectus femoris
Gracilis, Soleus, Temporalis, Trapezius, Peroneus brevis, SCM

mathes_nahai.pattern: Two dominant pedicles (either can sustain muscle)
mathes_nahai.examples: Gluteus maximus, Rectus abdominis, Serratus anterior, Semimembranosus
Sartorius, Tibialis anterior, Extensor hallucis longus, External oblique

mathes_nahai.pattern: One dominant pedicle plus secondary segmental pedicles

cormack_lamberty.pattern: Multiple fasciocutaneous perforators entering base of flap and oriented along longitudinal fascial plexus
Single moderate-sized fasciocutaneous perforator reliable enough to support an island or free flap
Multiple small perforators passing along an intermuscular septum from a deep source artery
cormack_lamberty.examples: Radial forearm (RFFF), Lateral arm, Posterior interosseous (PIA)

cormack_lamberty.pattern: Osteomyofasciocutaneous extension of Type C incorporating adjacent muscle and bone
cormack_lamberty.examples: Osteocutaneous radial forearm, Free fibula osteocutaneous

nakajima.pattern: Direct cutaneous artery piercing fascia directly to skin
Direct septocutaneous perforator traversing intermuscular septum
Direct cutaneous branch of muscular vessel piercing fascia adjacent to muscle
Perforating cutaneous branch of muscular vessel (classic musculocutaneous perforator)
nakajima.examples: DIEP, MSAP, SGAP, PAP, musculocutaneous ALT

nakajima.pattern: Septocutaneous perforator feeding deep fascial plexus before skin
nakajima.examples: Lower leg fasciocutaneous / PTAP / peroneal perforator

nakajima.pattern: Musculocutaneous perforator feeding deep fascial plexus extensively
nakajima.examples: Reverse sural / adipofascial lower extremity flaps

gent_consensus.detail: A vessel that pierces the deep fascia to reach the skin. Direct cutaneous vessels bypass deep fascia.
Muscle (musculocutaneous) perforators traverse muscle before piercing fascia; septal (septocutaneous) perforators travel exclusively in intermuscular septa.
Name the flap after its nutrient source vessel (e.g., DIEP, TDAP, SGAP, MSAP, PAP) rather than the underlying muscle, adding anatomical region if ambiguous (e.g., ALT).
Clarifies direct vs. indirect perforators and defines propeller flaps by eccentric perforator pivot rotation (typically 90°–180°).

reconstructive_ladder.indication: Small concave defects (medial canthus, fingertip without bone) or contaminated wounds awaiting demarcation
Tension-free wound edges along RSTL with healthy vascularized tissue
Well-vascularized wound bed without exposed bare bone, cartilage, tendon, or hardware
Exposed vital structures or need for color/texture match using adjacent laxity
reconstructive_ladder.examples: Limberg rhomboid, Zitelli bilobed, Z-plasty, Keystone

reconstructive_ladder.indication: Moderate defects within reliable vascular arc of rotation
reconstructive_ladder.examples: Gastrocnemius, Pectoralis major, Paramedian forehead, VRAM

reconstructive_ladder.indication: Large, composite, irradiated, osseous, or distal-third defects requiring distant uninjured tissue
reconstructive_ladder.examples: ALT, DIEP, Free Fibula, RFFF, Gracilis
